The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.
Summary of Restricted Stock Unit Activity
At the end of 2024, 7,278,000 shares were available to be granted as RSUs, and the following awards, adjusted for the effects of the special
dividend, were outstanding:
• 2,677,000 time-based RSUs, which vest upon continued employment or service over specified periods of time; and
• 122,000 performance-based RSUs, of which 95,000 were granted to executive officers subject to the determination of the attainment of
performance targets for 2024, which occurred in September 2024. At that time, depending upon long-service terms, at least 33% of the
units vested. The remaining awards vest upon continued employment over specified periods of time. Please refer to Note 1 for
accelerated vesting requirements.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

Our members may utilize their memberships at all of our warehouses and e-commerce sites. Gold Star memberships are available to individuals;
Business memberships are limited to businesses, including individuals with a business license, retail sales license, or comparable document.
Business members may add additional cardholders (affiliates), to which the same annual fee applies. Affiliates are not available for Gold Star
members. During fiscal 2024, our annual fee for these memberships was $60 in the U.S. and varies in other countries. All paid memberships
include a free household card.
Paid members (except affiliates) were eligible to upgrade to an Executive membership in the U.S., for an additional annual fee of $60. Executive
memberships are also available in Canada, Mexico, the U.K., Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and Australia, for which the additional fee varies. Executive
members earn a 2% reward on qualified purchases (generally up to a maximum reward of $1,000 per year), redeemable at Costco warehouses.
The sales penetration of Executive members represented approximately 73.3% of worldwide net sales in 2024.
Our member renewal rate was 92.9% in the U.S. and Canada and 90.5% worldwide at the end of 2024. The majority of members renew within
six months following their renewal date. Our renewal rate, which excludes affiliates of Business members, is a trailing calculation that captures
renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. Our membership counts include active memberships as well as
memberships that have not renewed within the 12 months prior to the reporting date.

To compute the unadjusted EBITDA Margin for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024, we need to calculate EBITDA (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization) and then divide it by Total Revenue.

### Step-by-Step Calculation:

1. **Identify Operating Income:**
   - From the financial statements, the operating income for 2024 is $9,285 million.

2. **Add Back Interest Expense:**
   - The interest expense for 2024 is $(169) million.
   - Add back this interest to the operating income:
     \[
     9,285 + 169 = 9,454 \text{ million}
     \]

3. **Add Back Depreciation and Amortization:**
   - From the cash flow statement (under Operating Activities), depreciation and amortization expense for 2024 is $2,237 million.
   - Add this to the previous total:
     \[
     9,454 + 2,237 = 11,691 \text{ million}
     \]

Thus, **EBITDA** (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization) for 2024 is $11,691 million.

### Calculate EBITDA Margin:

The EBITDA Margin is calculated by dividing the EBITDA by Total Revenue:
\[
\text{EBITDA Margin} = \frac{\text{EBITDA}}{\text{Total Revenue}}
\]

For 2024:
- **Total Revenue** = $254,453 million
- **EBITDA** = $11,691 million

Now calculate the margin:
\[
\text{EBITDA Margin} = \frac{11,691}{254,453} \times 100 \approx 4.6%
\]

### Conclusion:

The unadjusted EBITDA Margin for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is approximately **4.6%**.

To determine if the Operating Profit Margin is greater in 2024 compared to 2023, we need to calculate the operating profit margin for both years. The formula for Operating Profit Margin is:

\[ \text{Operating Profit Margin} = \left( \frac{\text{Operating Income}}{\text{Total Revenue}} \right) \times 100 \]

### Calculations

**For 2024:**
- **Operating Income:** $9,285 million
- **Total Revenue:** $254,453 million

\[ \text{Operating Profit Margin (2024)} = \left( \frac{9,285}{254,453} \right) \times 100 = 3.65\% \]

**For 2023:**
- **Operating Income:** $8,114 million
- **Total Revenue:** $242,290 million

\[ \text{Operating Profit Margin (2023)} = \left( \frac{8,114}{242,290} \right) \times 100 = 3.35\% \]

### Conclusion
The Operating Profit Margin for 2024 is **3.65%**, while it was **3.35%** in 2023. Therefore, the Operating Profit Margin is indeed greater in 2024 compared to 2023.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

• 122,000 performance-based RSUs, of which 95,000 were granted to executive officers subject to the determination of the attainment of
performance targets for 2024, which occurred in September 2024. At that time, depending upon long-service terms, at least 33% of the
units vested. The remaining awards vest upon continued employment over specified periods of time. Please refer to Note 1 for

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

Our members may utilize their memberships at all of our warehouses and e-commerce sites. Gold Star memberships are available to individuals;
Business memberships are limited to businesses, including individuals with a business license, retail sales license, or comparable document.
Business members may add additional cardholders (affiliates), to which the same annual fee applies. Affiliates are not available for Gold Star
members. During fiscal 2024, our annual fee for these memberships was $60 in the U.S. and varies in other countries. All paid memberships
include a free household card.
Paid members (except affiliates) were eligible to upgrade to an Executive membership in the U.S., for an additional annual fee of $60. Executive
memberships are also available in Canada, Mexico, the U.K., Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and Australia, for which the additional fee varies. Executive
members earn a 2% reward on qualified purchases (generally up to a maximum reward of $1,000 per year), redeemable at Costco warehouses.
The sales penetration of Executive members represented approximately 73.3% of worldwide net sales in 2024.
Our member renewal rate was 92.9% in the U.S. and Canada and 90.5% worldwide at the end of 2024. The majority of members renew within
six months following their renewal date. Our renewal rate, which excludes affiliates of Business members, is a trailing calculation that captures
renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. Our membership counts include active memberships as well as
memberships that have not renewed within the 12 months prior to the reporting date.

Goodwill represents the excess of acquisition cost over the fair value of the net assets acquired and is not subject to amortization. The Company
reviews goodwill annually in the fourth quarter for impairment or when circumstances indicate carrying value may exceed the fair value. This
evaluation is performed at the reporting unit level. If a qualitative assessment indicates that it is more likely than not that the fair value is less
than carrying value, a quantitative analysis is completed using either the income or market approach, or a combination of both. The income
approach estimates fair value based on expected discounted future cash flows, while the market approach uses comparable public companies
and transactions to develop metrics to be applied to historical and expected future operating results.

#### 1. Identify Net Income Attributable to Costco (Basic)

#### 2. Identify Basic EPS
From the per share data provided in the financial statements:

#### 3. Calculate the Number of Shares Outstanding (Basic)
Using the formula for EPS:
\[
\text{Basic EPS} = \frac{\text{Net Income Attributable to Costco}}{\text{Number of shares outstanding (basic)}}
\]
Solving for the number of shares:
\[
\text{Number of shares outstanding (basic)} = \frac{\$7,367}{\$16.59} \approx 444,280,000
\]

#### 4. Determine Market Price per Share
The given stock price is \$940.

#### 5. Calculate the P/E Ratio (Basic EPS)
\[
\text{P/E Ratio} = \frac{\text{Market Price per Share}}{\text{EPS}}
\]
Substituting the values:
\[
\text{P/E Ratio} = \frac{940}{16.59} \approx 56.73
\]

### Final Answer

The P/E ratio for Costco Wholesale Corporation using Basic EPS for the year ending September 1, 2024 is approximately **56.73**.

To compute the Market Value of Equity (MVE) for Costco Wholesale Corporation as of September 1, 2024, we need to follow these steps:

### Step 1: Calculate Fully Diluted Shares Outstanding

**Fully diluted shares outstanding** includes all common stock plus potentially dilutive securities such as options, RSUs, and convertible bonds. For this context, we focus on the outstanding RSUs.

From the given data:
- **Outstanding RSUs at the end of 2024**: 2,799,000 shares
- **Shares for vested but not yet delivered RSUs**: Approximately 908,000 shares (these are included in the outstanding balance)
- **Available to be granted as RSUs**: 7,278,000 shares (not dilutive until issued)

To calculate fully diluted shares:
\[ \text{Fully Diluted Shares} = \text{Basic Shares Outstanding} + \text{Outstanding RSUs} - \text{RSUs Vested but not yet delivered} \]

Given:
- Basic Shares Outstanding: 443,126,000 (from the Balance Sheet)
  
\[ 
\text{Fully Diluted Shares} = 443,126,000 + 2,799,000 - 908,000 
= 445,017,000
\]

### Step 2: Compute the Market Value of Equity

**Market Value of Equity (MVE)** is calculated as:
\[ \text{MVE} = \text{Fully Diluted Shares} \times \text{Stock Price} \]

Given Stock Price:
- Costco Stock Price on September 1, 2024: $940 per share

Now calculate MVE:

\[
\text{MVE} = 445,017,000 \text{ shares} \times \$940/\text{share}
= \$418,361,580,000
\]

### Final Answer:
The Market Value of Equity for Costco Wholesale Corporation as of September 1, 2024 is approximately **$418.36 billion**.

To estimate the cost of equity for Costco Wholesale Corporation using the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM) for the year 2024, we can use the following formula:

\[ \text{Cost of Equity} = R_f + \beta (R_m - R_f) \]

Where:
- \( R_f \) is the risk-free rate.
- \( \beta \) is the beta coefficient of the stock.
- \( R_m \) is the expected market return.

Given the data:

1. **Risk-Free Rate (\( R_f \))**: 4.617% (10-year Treasury yield)
2. **Market Return (\( R_m \))**: 11%
3. **Beta (\( \beta \))**: 0.79

Now, substitute the values into the CAPM formula:

\[ \text{Cost of Equity} = 4.617\% + 0.79 (11\% - 4.617\%) \]

Calculate the market risk premium (\( R_m - R_f \)):

\[ R_m - R_f = 11\% - 4.617\% = 6.383\% \]

Next, multiply the beta by the market risk premium:

\[ 0.79 \times 6.383\% = 5.02\% \]

Finally, add this product to the risk-free rate:

\[ \text{Cost of Equity} = 4.617\% + 5.02\% = 9.637\% \]

Therefore, the estimated cost of equity for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is approximately **9.64%**.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.
Summary of Restricted Stock Unit Activity
At the end of 2024, 7,278,000 shares were available to be granted as RSUs, and the following awards, adjusted for the effects of the special
dividend, were outstanding:
• 2,677,000 time-based RSUs, which vest upon continued employment or service over specified periods of time; and
• 122,000 performance-based RSUs, of which 95,000 were granted to executive officers subject to the determination of the attainment of
performance targets for 2024, which occurred in September 2024. At that time, depending upon long-service terms, at least 33% of the
units vested. The remaining awards vest upon continued employment over specified periods of time. Please refer to Note 1 for
accelerated vesting requirements.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash

The sales penetration of Executive members represented approximately 73.3% of worldwide net sales in 2024.

To calculate the Operating Deferred Tax Asset, net of deferred tax liabilities for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024:

1. **Deferred Tax Assets:**
   - Equity compensation: $96 million
   - Deferred income/membership fees: $313 million
   - Foreign tax credit carryforward: $315 million
   - Operating lease liabilities: $678 million
   - Accrued liabilities and reserves: $873 million
   
   Total deferred tax assets = $96 + $313 + $315 + $678 + $873 = **$2,275 million**

2. **Deferred Tax Liabilities:**
   - Property and equipment: $(948) million
   - Merchandise inventories: $(296) million
   - Operating lease right-of-use assets: $(652) million
   - Foreign branch deferreds: $(105) million
   
   Total deferred tax liabilities = $-(948 + 296 + 652 + 105) = **$(2,002) million**

3. **Net Operating Deferred Tax Asset:**
   
   Net operating deferred tax asset = Total deferred tax assets - Total deferred tax liabilities
   = $2,275 million - $(2,002) million = **$273 million**

Therefore, the Operating Deferred Tax Asset, net of deferred tax liabilities for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is **$273 million**.

To calculate the Operating Deferred Tax Asset, net of deferred tax liabilities for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2023:

1. **Identify Deferred Tax Assets**:
   - Equity compensation: $89 million
   - Deferred income/membership fees: $309 million
   - Foreign tax credit carry forward: $250 million
   - Operating lease liabilities: $678 million
   - Accrued liabilities and reserves: $761 million

   Total deferred tax assets = $89 + $309 + $250 + $678 + $761 = **$2,107** million.

2. **Identify Deferred Tax Liabilities**:
   - Property and equipment: ($867) million
   - Merchandise inventories: ($380) million
   - Operating lease right-of-use assets: ($655) million
   - Foreign branch deferreds: ($87) million

   Total deferred tax liabilities = -$867 + (-$380) + (-$655) + (-$87) = **-$1,989** million.

3. **Calculate Net Deferred Tax Asset**:
   Net deferred tax asset = Total deferred tax assets - Total deferred tax liabilities
                          = $2,107 million - ($1,989 million)
                          = $2,107 million + $1,989 million
                          = **$1,685** million.

Therefore, the Operating Deferred Tax Asset, net of deferred tax liabilities for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2023 is **$1,685 million**.

The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at

amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain

To determine the excess cash for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024, we need to follow these steps:

1. **Calculate Operating Cash**:
   - Operating cash is defined as the minimum between taking 2% of revenue and the actual cash on hand.

   From the balance sheet:
   - Total Revenue (Net sales + Membership fees) for 2024 = $254,453 million
   - Cash and cash equivalents at the end of 2024 = $9,906 million

   Calculate 2% of total revenue:
   \[
   0.02 \times 254,453 = 5,089.06 \text{ million dollars}
   \]

2. **Determine Operating Cash**:
   - Operating cash is the minimum between $5,089.06 million and $9,906 million.
   - Therefore, operating cash = $5,089.06 million.

3. **Calculate Excess Cash**:
   - Excess cash = Actual cash on hand – Operating cash
   \[
   9,906 - 5,089.06 = 4,816.94 \text{ million dollars}
   \]

Thus, the excess cash in 2024 is **$4,816.94 million**.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. Our membership counts include active memberships as well as

reviews goodwill annually in the fourth quarter for impairment or when circumstances indicate carrying value may exceed the fair value. This

approach estimates fair value based on expected discounted future cash flows, while the market approach uses comparable public companies

Net sales increased $11,915 or 5% during 2024. The improvement was attributable to an increase in comparable sales and sales at new
warehouses opened in 2023 and 2024, partially offset by the impact of one less week of sales in 2024. Sales increased $10,639, or 6% in core
merchandise categories, increasing in all categories. Sales increased $1,276, or 3% in warehouse ancillary and other businesses, led by
pharmacy, partially offset by a decrease in gasoline.
During 2024, the volume of gasoline sold increased approximately 1%, positively impacting net sales by $400, or 17 basis points, which includes
the impact of one less week of sales in 2024. Lower gasoline prices negatively impacted net sales by $917, or 39 basis points, compared to
2023, with a 3% decrease in the average price per gallon. Changes in foreign currencies relative to the U.S. dollar negatively impacted net sales
by approximately $474, 20 basis points, compared to 2023, attributable to our Canadian and Other International operations.
Comparable Sales
Comparable sales increased 5% during 2024 and were positively impacted by an increase in shopping frequency, partially offset by a slight
decrease in average ticket.

To calculate the ARPU (Average Revenue Per User) for Costco Wholesale Corporation for 2024, we need to use the total revenue from both net sales and membership fees divided by the total number of cardholders.

### Step-by-Step Calculation:

1. **Total Revenue:**
   - Net Sales: $249,625 million
   - Membership Fees: $4,828 million
   - Total Revenue = $249,625 + $4,828 = $254,453 million

2. **Total Number of Cardholders:**
   - At the end of 2024, total cardholders were 136,800 thousand (or 136,800,000).

### ARPU Calculation:

\[ \text{ARPU} = \frac{\text{Total Revenue}}{\text{Number of Cardholders}} \]

\[ \text{ARPU} = \frac{254,453}{136,800} \approx 1.86 \]

Therefore, the ARPU for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is approximately **$1,860** per user (since each cardholder is counted as a unique user).

2. **Identify Total Current Liabilities (CL) from the Balance Sheet:**

3. **Calculate Operating Working Capital (OWC):**
\[ OWC = CA - CL \]
\[ OWC = \$35,879\text{M} - \$33,583\text{M} = \$2,296\text{M} \]

Thus, the operating working capital for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2023 is **$2.296 billion**.

To calculate the change in operating working capital from 2023 to 2024 using 2% of revenue as max potential operating cash:

### Step-by-Step Calculation

1. **Identify Current Assets and Liabilities:**
   - **Current Assets (2024):** $34,246 million
   - **Current Assets (2023):** $35,879 million
   - **Current Liabilities (2024):** $35,464 million
   - **Current Liabilities (2023):** $33,583 million

2. **Calculate Operating Working Capital:**
   \[
   \text{Operating Working Capital} = \text{Current Assets} - \text{Current Liabilities}
   \]

   For 2024:
   \[
   \text{Operating Working Capital}_{2024} = \$34,246M - \$35,464M = -\$1,218M
   \]

   For 2023:
   \[
   \text{Operating Working Capital}_{2023} = \$35,879M - \$33,583M = \$2,296M
   \]

3. **Determine Change in Operating Working Capital:**
   \[
   \Delta \text{Operating Working Capital} = \text{Operating Working Capital}_{2024} - \text{Operating Working Capital}_{2023}
   \]
   \[
   \Delta \text{Operating Working Capital} = (-\$1,218M) - \$2,296M = -\$3,514M
   \]

### Verification with Cash Flow Data

The statement of cash flows shows:
- **Net cash provided by operating activities:**
  - 2024: $11,339 million
  - 2023: $11,068 million

The significant change in working capital directly impacts the operating cash flow. The large reduction (negative) in operating working capital aligns with a substantial increase in net cash provided by operating activities.

### Conclusion:
The change in operating working capital from 2023 to 2024 is **-$3,514 million**, indicating a significant use of working capital which contributes to higher operating cash flow.

\[ \text{Levered Free Cash Flow} = \text{Operating Cash Flow} - \text{Capital Expenditures} + \text{Non-cash Expenses} \]

From the provided financial statements:
- **Net cash provided by operating activities** (operating cash flow) for 2024 is $11,339 million.
- **Additions to property and equipment** (capital expenditures) for 2024 is $4,710 million.
- **Depreciation and amortization** (non-cash expenses) for 2024 is $2,237 million.

Using these figures:

\[ \text{Levered Free Cash Flow} = \$11,339 - \$4,710 + \$2,237 \]
\[ \text{Levered Free Cash Flow} = \$8,866 \]

Thus, the levered free cash flow for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is **$8,866 million**.

To calculate the Accounts Receivables Days (ARD) for Costco Wholesale Corporation for 2024, we use the following formula:

\[ \text{Accounts Receivable Days} = \frac{\text{(Net Sales / 365)}}{\text{Average Daily Receivables}} \times 100 \]

However, a more common and simpler way to express this calculation is:

\[ \text{Accounts Receivable Days} = \frac{\text{Receivables}}{\text{Net Credit Sales per Day}} \]

Where:
- **Net Credit Sales per Day** = Net Sales / 365
- **Receivables** are the net receivables at the end of the period.

From the provided data:

1. **Net Sales for 2024**: $249,625 million.
2. **Receivables (net) as of September 1, 2024**: $2,721 million.

First, calculate Net Credit Sales per Day:

\[ \text{Net Credit Sales per Day} = \frac{\$249,625}{365} \approx \$683.30 \text{ (in millions)} \]

Next, we use the formula to find ARD:

\[ \text{Accounts Receivable Days} = \frac{\$2,721}{\$683.30} \times 365 \approx 15.94 \text{ days} \]

Therefore, Accounts Receivables Days for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is approximately **15.94 days**.

To calculate the Accounts Payables Days for Costco Wholesale Corporation for 2024, we use the following formula:

\[ \text{Accounts Payables Days} = \frac{\text{Cost of Goods Sold (COGS)}}{\text{Average Daily Purchases}} \]

The COGS is derived from the Merchandise Costs provided in the Income Statement, which was $222,358 million for 2024. The Average Daily Purchases can be calculated by dividing the Cost of Goods Sold by the number of days in a year (assuming 365 days):

\[ \text{Average Daily Purchases} = \frac{\text{COGS}}{365} = \frac{222,358}{365} \approx 609.197 \text{ million dollars per day} \]

Next, we use the Accounts Payables figure from the Balance Sheet for 2024, which is $19,421 million.

Now, calculate the Accounts Payables Days:

\[ \text{Accounts Payables Days} = \frac{\text{Accounts Payables}}{\text{Average Daily Purchases}} = \frac{19,421}{609.197} \approx 31.85 \]

Therefore, the Accounts Payables Days for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is approximately **31.85 days**.

To calculate the Inventory Turnover for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024, we use the formula:

\[ \text{Inventory Turnover} = \frac{\text{Cost of Goods Sold (COGS)}}{\text{Average Inventory}} \]

From the provided financial statements:
- **Merchandise costs** (which is COGS) for 2024: $222,358 million
- **Merchandise inventories** at the end of 2024: $18,647 million
- **Merchandise inventories** at the end of 2023: $16,651 million

First, we need to calculate the average inventory for 2024:

\[ \text{Average Inventory} = \frac{\text{Inventory (end of 2024)} + \text{Inventory (end of 2023)}}{2} \]
\[ \text{Average Inventory} = \frac{18,647 + 16,651}{2} = \frac{35,298}{2} = 17,649 \text{ million dollars} \]

Next, we calculate the inventory turnover:

\[ \text{Inventory Turnover} = \frac{\text{Merchandise Costs}}{\text{Average Inventory}} = \frac{222,358}{17,649} \approx 12.59 \]

Therefore, Costco Wholesale Corporation's **Inventory Turnover for 2024** is approximately 12.59.

To find the average total assets for 2024, we need to consider the total assets at the beginning and end of the period:

\[ \text{Average Total Assets} = \frac{\text{Total Assets for 2024} + \text{Total Assets for 2023}}{2} \]

\[ \text{Average Total Assets} = \frac{69,831 + 68,994}{2} = \frac{138,825}{2} = 69,412.5 \text{ million dollars} \]

### Step 3: Calculate Asset Turnover
Now we can plug the values into the asset turnover formula:

\[ \text{Asset Turnover for 2024} = \frac{249,625}{69,412.5} \approx 3.59 \]

The Asset Turnover ratio for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is approximately **3.59**.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

performance targets for 2024, which occurred in September 2024. At that time, depending upon long-service terms, at least 33% of the

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

Our members may utilize their memberships at all of our warehouses and e-commerce sites. Gold Star memberships are available to individuals;
Business memberships are limited to businesses, including individuals with a business license, retail sales license, or comparable document.
Business members may add additional cardholders (affiliates), to which the same annual fee applies. Affiliates are not available for Gold Star
members. During fiscal 2024, our annual fee for these memberships was $60 in the U.S. and varies in other countries. All paid memberships
include a free household card.
Paid members (except affiliates) were eligible to upgrade to an Executive membership in the U.S., for an additional annual fee of $60. Executive
memberships are also available in Canada, Mexico, the U.K., Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and Australia, for which the additional fee varies. Executive
members earn a 2% reward on qualified purchases (generally up to a maximum reward of $1,000 per year), redeemable at Costco warehouses.
The sales penetration of Executive members represented approximately 73.3% of worldwide net sales in 2024.
Our member renewal rate was 92.9% in the U.S. and Canada and 90.5% worldwide at the end of 2024. The majority of members renew within
six months following their renewal date. Our renewal rate, which excludes affiliates of Business members, is a trailing calculation that captures
renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. Our membership counts include active memberships as well as
memberships that have not renewed within the 12 months prior to the reporting date.

Goodwill represents the excess of acquisition cost over the fair value of the net assets acquired and is not subject to amortization. The Company
reviews goodwill annually in the fourth quarter for impairment or when circumstances indicate carrying value may exceed the fair value. This
evaluation is performed at the reporting unit level. If a qualitative assessment indicates that it is more likely than not that the fair value is less
than carrying value, a quantitative analysis is completed using either the income or market approach, or a combination of both. The income
approach estimates fair value based on expected discounted future cash flows, while the market approach uses comparable public companies
and transactions to develop metrics to be applied to historical and expected future operating results.
